Just with regular wear, airliners need a lot of replacement parts and inspections (not to mention a highly-trained crew of Pilots, Traffic Controllers, technicians, etc.) Depending on how it's built (magnetic rail in a vacuum tube for example) the only moving parts would be the pumps and the vehicles themselves and the only crew would be specialists and operators at the stations and possibly the pumps. There's no data yet, but when I say conceivably safer I mean, overall, there seems to be far less that can go wrong with this tube than could go wrong with an airline even 'tho airlines take very lengthy measures to make sure they don't happen. The technology has existed for a long time, it just hasn't been put together until now.

Hopefully if one of these prototype companies gets it right we can get some approximations of how safely this can be done for what speeds/loads etc. and then we can worry about where it would be the most useful.
